why.body:
Look at the cranes. Stockport's Mayoral Development Corporation — the first in the country to expand its boundary across the whole town centre, now covering 410 acres — has already delivered 1,200 homes with another 1,500 in the pipeline. The Interchange opened in March 2024 with its two-acre park. Weir Mill's transformation into 253 apartments completes in spring 2026. The Cheadle Eco Business Park adds 115,000 sq ft of sustainable commercial space. This is not incremental change; it's a town being rebuilt.

Rebuilt towns redraw search behaviour. New residents search for everything — dentists, takeaways, trades, schools — with no loyalty to incumbents. New firms need suppliers. Commuters priced out of Manchester arrive with Manchester expectations and Stockport postcodes. Every one of those searches is contestable right now, because most Stockport businesses are still running the same websites they had in 2019. The gap between the town's growth and its digital presence is the opportunity.
why.heading: Stockport Is Growing Faster Than Its Search Results
